decorations.colors.en: Controls whether editor file decorations should use colors.

dirty.en: `${dirty}`: an indicator for when the active editor has unsaved changes.

doubleClickTabToToggleEditorGroupSizes.en: Controls how the editor group is resized when double clicking on a tab. This value is ignored when {0} is not set to {1}.
comment: {0}, {1} will be a setting name rendered as a link

dragToOpenWindow.en: Controls if editors can be dragged out of the window to open them in a new window. Press and hold the `Alt` key while dragging to toggle this dynamically.

editorActionsLocation.en: Controls where the editor actions are shown.

editorOpenPositioning.en: Controls where editors open. Select {0} or {1} to open editors to the left or right of the currently active one. Select {2} or {3} to open editors independently from the currently active one.
comment: {0}, {1}, {2}, {3} will be a setting name rendered as a link

enableMenuBarMnemonics.en: Controls whether the main menus can be opened via Alt-key shortcuts. Disabling mnemonics allows to bind these Alt-key shortcuts to editor commands instead.

enableNaturalLanguageSearch.en: Controls whether the command palette should include similar commands. You must have an extension installed that provides Natural Language support.

enablePreview.en: Controls whether preview mode is used when editors open. There is a maximum of one preview mode editor per editor group. This editor displays its filename in italics on its tab or title label and in the Open Editors view. Its contents will be replaced by the next editor opened in preview mode. Making a change in a preview mode editor will persist it, as will a double-click on its label, or the 'Keep Open' option in its label context menu. Opening a file from Explorer with a double-click persists its editor immediately.

enablePreviewFromCodeNavigation.en: Controls whether editors remain in preview when a code navigation is started from them. Preview editors do not stay open, and are reused until explicitly set to be kept open (via double-click or editing). This value is ignored when {0} is not set to {1}.
comment: {0}, {1} will be a setting name rendered as a link

enablePreviewFromQuickOpen.en: Controls whether editors opened from Quick Open show as preview editors. Preview editors do not stay open, and are reused until explicitly set to be kept open (via double-click or editing). When enabled, hold Ctrl before selection to open an editor as a non-preview. This value is ignored when {0} is not set to {1}.
comment: {0}, {1} will be a setting name rendered as a link

exclude.en: Configure paths or [glob patterns](https://aka.ms/vscode-glob-patterns) for excluding files from the local file history. Glob patterns are always evaluated relative to the path of the workspace folder unless they are absolute paths. Changing this setting has no effect on existing local file history entries.

focusedView.en: `${focusedView}`: the name of the view that is currently focused.

focusRecentEditorAfterClose.en: Controls whether editors are closed in most recently used order or from left to right.

folderName.en: `${folderName}`: name of the workspace folder the file is contained in (e.g. myFolder).

folderPath.en: `${folderPath}`: file path of the workspace folder the file is contained in (e.g. /Users/Development/myFolder).

fontAliasing.en: Controls font aliasing method in the workbench.

highlightModifiedTabs.en: Controls whether a top border is drawn on tabs for editors that have unsaved changes. This value is ignored when {0} is not set to {1}.
comment: {0}, {1} will be a setting name rendered as a link

layoutcontrol.type.both.en: Shows both the dropdown and toggle buttons.

layoutcontrol.type.menu.en: Shows a single button with a dropdown of layout options.

layoutcontrol.type.toggles.en: Shows several buttons for toggling the visibility of the panels and side bar.

layoutControlEnabled.en: Controls whether the layout control is shown in the custom title bar. This setting only has an effect when {0} is not set to {1}.
comment: {0}, {1} is a placeholder for a setting identifier.

layoutControlEnabledWeb.en: Controls whether the layout control in the title bar is shown.

layoutControlType.en: Controls whether the layout control in the custom title bar is displayed as a single menu button or with multiple UI toggles.

limitEditorsEnablement.en: Controls if the number of opened editors should be limited or not. When enabled, less recently used editors will close to make space for newly opening editors.

limitEditorsExcludeDirty.en: Controls if the maximum number of opened editors should exclude dirty editors for counting towards the configured limit.

limitEditorsMaximum.en: Controls the maximum number of opened editors. Use the {0} setting to control this limit per editor group or across all groups.

localHistoryEnabled.en: Controls whether local file history is enabled. When enabled, the file contents of an editor that is saved will be stored to a backup location to be able to restore or review the contents later. Changing this setting has no effect on existing local file history entries.

localHistoryMaxFileEntries.en: Controls the maximum number of local file history entries per file. When the number of local file history entries exceeds this number for a file, the oldest entries will be discarded.

localHistoryMaxFileSize.en: Controls the maximum size of a file (in KB) to be considered for local file history. Files that are larger will not be added to the local file history. Changing this setting has no effect on existing local file history entries.

menuBarVisibility.en: Control the visibility of the menu bar. A setting of 'toggle' means that the menu bar is hidden and a single press of the Alt key will show it. A setting of 'compact' will move the menu into the side bar.

menuBarVisibility.mac.en: Control the visibility of the menu bar. A setting of 'toggle' means that the menu bar is hidden and executing `Focus Application Menu` will show it. A setting of 'compact' will move the menu into the side bar.

mergeWindow.en: Configure an interval in seconds during which the last entry in local file history is replaced with the entry that is being added. This helps reduce the overall number of entries that are added, for example when auto save is enabled. This setting is only applied to entries that have the same source of origin. Changing this setting has no effect on existing local file history entries.

modernUI.en: Controls whether the Modern UI Update is enabled. When on, the side bars and bottom panel are shown as floating cards with rounded corners and gaps, and a set of refreshed workbench styles is applied, matching the Agents window design.

modernUIEditorTabStyle.en: Controls the editor tab style when {0} is enabled, and the chat and side-panel tab style in the Agents window. High contrast themes retain explicit selection and focus borders.
comment: {0} is a placeholder for a setting identifier.

modernUIEditorTabStyle.connected.en: Connect the active tab to the editor surface with an outside border and curved shoulders.

modernUIEditorTabStyle.pill.en: Show editor tabs as separate rounded pills.

modernUIUppercaseViewHeaders.en: Controls whether view headers, side bar titles, and panel tabs use uppercase text when {0} is enabled.
comment: {0} is a placeholder for a setting identifier.

mouseBackForwardToNavigate.en: Enables the use of mouse buttons four and five for commands 'Go Back' and 'Go Forward'.

navigationControlEnabled.en: Controls whether the navigation control is shown in the custom title bar. This setting only has an effect when {0} is not set to {1}.
comment: {0}, {1} is a placeholder for a setting identifier.

navigationControlEnabledWeb.en: Controls whether the navigation control in the title bar is shown.

navigationScope.en: Controls the scope of history navigation in editors for commands such as 'Go Back' and 'Go Forward'.

notificationsButton.en: Controls the visibility of the Notifications button in the title bar. Only applies when notifications are positioned at the top right.

notificationsPosition.en: Controls the position of the notification toasts and notification center.

openDefaultKeybindings.en: Controls whether opening keybinding settings also opens an editor showing all default keybindings.

openDefaultSettings.en: Controls whether opening settings also opens an editor showing all default settings.

openFilesInNewWindow.en:
Controls whether files should open in a new window when using a command line or file dialog.
Note that there can still be cases where this setting is ignored (e.g. when using the `--new-window` or `--reuse-window` command line option).

openFilesInNewWindowMac.en:
Controls whether files should open in a new window when using a command line or file dialog.
Note that there can still be cases where this setting is ignored (e.g. when using the `--new-window` or `--reuse-window` command line option).

openFoldersInNewWindow.en:
Controls whether folders should open in a new window or replace the last active window.
Note that there can still be cases where this setting is ignored (e.g. when using the `--new-window` or `--reuse-window` command line option).

panelDefaultLocation.en: Controls the default location of the panel (Terminal, Debug Console, Output, Problems) in a new workspace. It can either show at the bottom, top, right, or left of the editor area.

panelOpensMaximized.en: Controls whether the panel opens maximized. It can either always open maximized, never open maximized, or open to the last state it was in before being closed.

panelShowLabels.en: Controls whether activity items in the panel title are shown as label or icon.

perEditorGroup.en: Controls if the limit of maximum opened editors should apply per editor group or across all editor groups.

pinnedTabSizing.en: Controls the size of pinned editor tabs. Pinned tabs are sorted to the beginning of all opened tabs and typically do not close until unpinned. This value is ignored when {0} is not set to {1}.
comment: {0}, {1} will be a setting name rendered as a link

preserveInput.en: Controls whether the last typed input to the command palette should be restored when opening it the next time.

problems.visibility.en: Controls whether the problems are visible throughout the editor and workbench.

profileName.en: `${profileName}`: name of the profile in which the workspace is opened (e.g. Data Science (Profile)). Ignored if default profile is used.

restoreOnStartup.en: Controls whether editors are restored on startup. When disabled, only dirty editors will be restored from the previous session.

restoreViewState.en: Restores the last editor view state (such as scroll position) when re-opening editors after they have been closed. Editor view state is stored per editor group and discarded when a group closes. Use the {0} setting to use the last known view state across all editor groups in case no previous view state was found for a editor group.

revealIfOpen.en: Controls whether an editor is revealed in any of the visible groups if opened. If disabled, an editor will prefer to open in the currently active editor group. If enabled, an already opened editor will be revealed instead of opened again in the currently active editor group. Note that there are some cases where this setting is ignored, such as when forcing an editor to open in a specific group or to the side of the currently active group.

rootName.en: `${rootName}`: name of the workspace with optional remote name and workspace indicator if applicable (e.g. myFolder, myRemoteFolder [SSH] or myWorkspace (Workspace)).

rootNameShort.en: `${rootNameShort}`: shortened name of the workspace without suffixes (e.g. myFolder, myRemoteFolder or myWorkspace).

rootPath.en: `${rootPath}`: file path of the opened workspace or folder (e.g. /Users/Development/myWorkspace).

scrollToSwitchTabs.en: Controls whether scrolling over tabs will open them or not. By default tabs will only reveal upon scrolling, but not open. You can press and hold the Shift-key while scrolling to change this behavior for that duration. This value is ignored when {0} is not set to {1}.
comment: {0}, {1} will be a setting name rendered as a link

secondarySideBarDefaultVisibility.en: Controls the default visibility of the secondary side bar in workspaces or empty windows that are opened for the first time. Can be overridden by the agent sessions startup editor setting.

secondarySideBarForceMaximized.en: Controls whether the secondary side bar is enforced to always show maximized on startup and when there are no open editors, in layouts that support a maximized secondary side bar.

secondarySideBarShowLabels.en: Controls whether activity items in the secondary side bar title are shown as label or icon. This setting only has an effect when {0} is not set to {1}.

separator.en: `${separator}`: a conditional separator (" - ") that only shows when surrounded by variables with values or static text.

settings.editor.desc.en: Determines which Settings editor to use by default.

settings.showAISearchToggle.en: Controls whether the AI search results toggle is shown in the search bar in the Settings editor after doing a search and once AI search results are available.

shadows.en: Controls whether shadow effects are shown around the side panels and other workbench elements.

sharedViewState.en: Preserves the most recent editor view state (such as scroll position) across all editor groups and restores that if no specific editor view state is found for the editor group.

showAskInChat.en: Controls whether the command palette shows 'Ask in Chat' option at the bottom.

showEditorTabs.en: Controls whether opened editors should show as individual tabs, one single large tab or if the title area should not be shown.

showIcons.en: Controls whether opened editors should show with an icon or not. This requires a file icon theme to be enabled as well.

showTabIndex.en: When enabled, will show the tab index. This value is ignored when {0} is not set to {1}.
comment: {0}, {1} will be a setting name rendered as a link

sideBarLocation.en: Controls the location of the primary side bar and activity bar. They can either show on the left or right of the workbench. The secondary side bar will show on the opposite side of the workbench.

sideBySideDirection.en: Controls the default direction of editors that are opened side by side (for example, from the Explorer). By default, editors will open on the right hand side of the currently active one. If changed to `down`, the editors will open below the currently active one. This also impacts the split editor action in the editor toolbar.

splitInGroupLayout.en: Controls the layout for when an editor is split in an editor group to be either vertical or horizontal.

splitOnDragAndDrop.en: Controls if editor groups can be split from drag and drop operations by dropping an editor or file on the edges of the editor area.

splitSizing.en: Controls the size of editor groups when splitting them.

statusBarVisibility.en: Controls the visibility of the status bar at the bottom of the workbench.

suggestCommands.en: Controls whether the command palette should have a list of commonly used commands.

swipeToNavigate.en: Navigate between open files using three-finger swipe horizontally. Note that System Preferences > Trackpad > More Gestures > 'Swipe between pages' must be set to 'Swipe with two or three fingers'.

tabActionLocation.en: Controls the position of the editor's tabs action buttons (close, unpin). This value is ignored when {0} is not set to {1}.
comment: {0} will be a setting name rendered as a link

tabDescription.en: Controls the format of the label for an editor.

tabScrollbarHeight.en: Controls the height of the scrollbars used for tabs and breadcrumbs in the editor title area.

tabSizing.en: Controls the size of editor tabs. This value is ignored when {0} is not set to {1}.
comment: {0}, {1} will be a setting name rendered as a link

tips.enabled.en: When enabled, will show the watermark tips when no editor is open.

titleScrollbarVisibility.en: Controls the visibility of the scrollbars used for tabs and breadcrumbs in the editor title area.

untitledLabelFormat.en: Controls the format of the label for an untitled editor.

useModal.en: Controls whether editors open in a modal overlay.

useModal.all.en: All editors open in a centered modal overlay.

useModal.off.en: Editors never open in a modal overlay.

useModal.some.en: Certain editors such as Settings and Keyboard Shortcuts may open in a centered modal overlay.

useSplitJSON.en: Controls whether to use the split JSON editor when editing settings as JSON.

viewVisibility.en: Controls the visibility of view header actions. View header actions may either be always visible, or only visible when that view is focused or hovered over.

window.commandCenter.en: Show command launcher together with the window title. This setting only has an effect when {0} is not set to {1}.
comment: {0}, {1} is a placeholder for a setting identifier.

window.commandCenterWeb.en: Show command launcher together with the window title.

window.confirmBeforeClose.always.web.en: Always try to ask for confirmation. Note that browsers may still decide to close a tab or window without confirmation.

window.confirmBeforeClose.keyboardOnly.en: Only ask for confirmation if a keybinding was used.

window.confirmBeforeClose.keyboardOnly.w.en: Only ask for confirmation if a keybinding was used to close the window. Note that detection may not be possible in some cases.

window.confirmBeforeClose.never.web.en: Never explicitly ask for confirmation unless data loss is imminent.

window.menuBarVisibility.classic.en: Menu is displayed at the top of the window and only hidden in full screen mode.

window.menuBarVisibility.compact.en: Menu is displayed as a compact button in the side bar. This value is ignored when {0} is {1} and {2} is either {3} or {4}.
comment: {0}, {1} is a placeholder for a setting identifier.

window.menuBarVisibility.compact.web.en: Menu is displayed as a compact button in the side bar.

window.menuBarVisibility.toggle.en: Menu is hidden but can be displayed at the top of the window via the Alt key.

window.menuBarVisibility.toggle.mac.en: Menu is hidden but can be displayed at the top of the window by executing the `Focus Application Menu` command.

window.menuBarVisibility.visible.en: Menu is always visible at the top of the window even in full screen mode.

window.openFilesInNewWindow.default.en: Files will open in a new window unless picked from within the application (e.g. via the File menu).

window.openFilesInNewWindow.defaultMac.en: Files will open in the window with the files' folder open or the last active window unless opened via the Dock or from Finder.

window.openFilesInNewWindow.off.en: Files will open in the window with the files' folder open or the last active window.

window.openFilesInNewWindow.on.en: Files will open in a new window.

window.openFoldersInNewWindow.default.en: Folders will open in a new window unless a folder is picked from within the application (e.g. via the File menu).

window.openFoldersInNewWindow.off.en: Folders will replace the last active window.

window.openFoldersInNewWindow.on.en: Folders will open in a new window.

windowDensityLayout.en: Controls the spacing density of the workbench layout. Only applies when {0} is enabled.
comment: {0} is a placeholder for a setting identifier.

windowDensityLayout.compact.en: Removes the gaps between workbench parts and reduces their internal spacing to provide more room for content.

windowDensityLayout.default.en: Uses the standard spacing between workbench parts.

windowTitle.en: Controls the window title based on the current context such as the opened workspace or active editor. Variables are substituted based on the context:

workbench.activityBar.iconClickBehavior..en: Focus the Primary Side Bar if the clicked item is already visible.
Hide the Primary Side Bar if the clicked item is already visible.

workbench.activityBar.location.bottom.en: Show the Activity Bar at the bottom of the Primary and Secondary Side Bars.

workbench.activityBar.location.default.en: Show the Activity Bar on the side of the Primary Side Bar and on top of the Secondary Side Bar.

workbench.activityBar.location.hide.en: Hide the Activity Bar in the Primary and Secondary Side Bars.

workbench.activityBar.location.top.en: Show the Activity Bar on top of the Primary and Secondary Side Bars.

workbench.editor.doubleClickTabToToggleE.en: The editor group takes as much space as possible by making all other editor groups as small as possible.
All other editor groups are hidden and the current editor group is maximized to take up the entire editor area.
No editor group is resized when double clicking on a tab.

workbench.editor.editorActionsLocation.d.en: Show editor actions in the window title bar when {0} is set to {1}. Otherwise, editor actions are shown in the editor tab bar.
comment: {0} will be a setting name rendered as a link

workbench.editor.editorActionsLocation.t.en: Show editor actions in the window title bar. If {0} is set to {1}, editor actions are hidden.
comment: {0} will be a setting name rendered as a link

workbench.editor.empty.hint.en: Controls if the empty editor text hint should be visible in the editor.

workbench.editor.historyBasedLanguageDet.en: Enables use of editor history in language detection. This causes automatic language detection to favor languages that have been recently opened and allows for automatic language detection to operate with smaller inputs.

workbench.editor.label.dirname.en: `${dirname}`: name of the folder in which the file is located (e.g. `WORKSPACE_FOLDER/folder/file.txt -> folder`).

workbench.editor.label.enabled.en: Controls whether the custom workbench editor labels should be applied.

workbench.editor.label.filename.en: `${filename}`: name of the file without the file extension (e.g. `WORKSPACE_FOLDER/folder/file.txt -> file`).

workbench.editor.label.nthdirname.en: `${dirname(N)}`: name of the nth parent folder in which the file is located (e.g. `N=2: WORKSPACE_FOLDER/static/folder/file.txt -> WORKSPACE_FOLDER`). Folders can be picked from the start of the path by using negative numbers (e.g. `N=-1: WORKSPACE_FOLDER/folder/file.txt -> WORKSPACE_FOLDER`). If the __Item__ is an absolute pattern path, the first folder (`N=-1`) refers to the first folder in the absolute path, otherwise it corresponds to the workspace folder.

workbench.editor.label.nthextname.en: `${extname(N)}`: the nth extension of the file separated by '.' (e.g. `N=2: WORKSPACE_FOLDER/folder/file.ext1.ext2.ext3 -> ext1`). Extension can be picked from the start of the extension by using negative numbers (e.g. `N=-1: WORKSPACE_FOLDER/folder/file.ext1.ext2.ext3 -> ext2`).

workbench.editor.label.patterns.en: Controls the rendering of the editor label. Each __Item__ is a pattern that matches a file path. Both relative and absolute file paths are supported. The relative path must include the WORKSPACE_FOLDER (e.g `WORKSPACE_FOLDER/src/**.tsx` or `*/src/**.tsx`). Absolute patterns must start with a `/`. In case multiple patterns match, the longest matching path will be picked. Each __Value__ is the template for the rendered editor when the __Item__ matches. Variables are substituted based on the context:

workbench.editor.label.template.en: The template which should be rendered when the pattern matches. May include the variables ${dirname}, ${filename} and ${extname}.

workbench.editor.labelFormat.default.en: Show the name of the file. When tabs are enabled and two files have the same name in one group the distinguishing sections of each file's path are added. When tabs are disabled, the path relative to the workspace folder is shown if the editor is active.

workbench.editor.labelFormat.long.en: Show the name of the file followed by its absolute path.

workbench.editor.labelFormat.medium.en: Show the name of the file followed by its path relative to the workspace folder.

workbench.editor.labelFormat.short.en: Show the name of the file followed by its directory name.

workbench.editor.languageDetection.en: Controls whether the language in a text editor is automatically detected unless the language has been explicitly set by the language picker. This can also be scoped by language so you can specify which languages you do not want to be switched off of. This is useful for languages like Markdown that often contain other languages that might trick language detection into thinking it's the embedded language and not Markdown.

workbench.editor.navigationScopeDefault.en: Navigate across all opened editors and editor groups.

workbench.editor.navigationScopeEditor.en: Navigate only in the active editor.

workbench.editor.navigationScopeEditorGr.en: Navigate only in editors of the active editor group.

workbench.editor.pinnedTabSizing.compact.en: A pinned tab will show in a compact form with only icon or first letter of the editor name.

workbench.editor.pinnedTabSizing.normal.en: A pinned tab inherits the look of non pinned tabs.

workbench.editor.pinnedTabSizing.shrink.en: A pinned tab shrinks to a compact fixed size showing parts of the editor name.

workbench.editor.pinnedTabsOnSeparateRow.en: When enabled, displays pinned tabs in a separate row above all other tabs. This value is ignored when {0} is not set to {1}.
comment: {0}, {1} will be a setting name rendered as a link

workbench.editor.preferBasedLanguageDete.en: When enabled, a language detection model that takes into account editor history will be given higher precedence.

workbench.editor.preventPinnedEditorClos.en: Controls whether pinned editors should close when keyboard or middle mouse click is used for closing.
Always prevent closing the pinned editor when using mouse middle click or keyboard.
Never prevent closing a pinned editor.
Prevent closing the pinned editor when using the keyboard.
Prevent closing the pinned editor when using mouse middle click.

workbench.editor.showLanguageDetectionHi.en: When enabled, shows a status bar Quick Fix when the editor language doesn't match detected content language.

workbench.editor.showTabs.multiple.en: Each editor is displayed as a tab in the editor title area.

workbench.editor.showTabs.none.en: The editor title area is not displayed.

workbench.editor.showTabs.single.en: The active editor is displayed as a single large tab in the editor title area.

workbench.editor.splitInGroupLayoutHoriz.en: Editors are positioned from left to right.

workbench.editor.splitInGroupLayoutVerti.en: Editors are positioned from top to bottom.

workbench.editor.splitSizingAuto.en: Splits the active editor group to equal parts, unless all editor groups are already in equal parts. In that case, splits all the editor groups to equal parts.

workbench.editor.splitSizingDistribute.en: Splits all the editor groups to equal parts.

workbench.editor.splitSizingSplit.en: Splits the active editor group to equal parts.

workbench.editor.tabActionCloseVisibilit.en: Controls the visibility of the tab close action button.

workbench.editor.tabActionReserveSpace.en: Controls whether Modern UI editor tabs always reserve space for tab action buttons. When disabled, clean tabs stay compact; tabs with persistent dirty or pinned indicators reserve space regardless.

workbench.editor.tabActionUnpinVisibilit.en: Controls the visibility of the tab unpin action button.

workbench.editor.tabHeight.en: Controls the height of editor tabs. Also applies to the title control bar when {0} is not set to {1}.
comment: {0}, {1} will be a setting name rendered as a link

workbench.editor.tabSizing.fit.en: Always keep tabs large enough to show the full editor label.

workbench.editor.tabSizing.fixed.en: Make all tabs the same size, while allowing them to get smaller when the available space is not enough to show all tabs at once.

workbench.editor.tabSizing.shrink.en: Allow tabs to get smaller when the available space is not enough to show all tabs at once.

workbench.editor.tabSizingFixedMaxWidth.en: Controls the maximum width of tabs when {0} size is set to {1}.
comment: {0}, {1} will be a setting name rendered as a link

workbench.editor.tabSizingFixedMinWidth.en: Controls the minimum width of tabs when {0} size is set to {1}.
comment: {0}, {1} will be a setting name rendered as a link

workbench.editor.titleScrollbarSizing.la.en: Increases the size, so it can be grabbed more easily with the mouse.

workbench.editor.titleScrollbarVisibilit.en: The horizontal scrollbar will be visible only when necessary.
The horizontal scrollbar will always be hidden.
The horizontal scrollbar will always be visible.

workbench.editor.untitled.labelFormat.co.en: The name of the untitled file is derived from the contents of its first line unless it has an associated file path. It will fallback to the name in case the line is empty or contains no word characters.

workbench.editor.untitled.labelFormat.na.en: The name of the untitled file is not derived from the contents of the file.

workbench.fontAliasing.antialiased.en: Smooth the font on the level of the pixel, as opposed to the subpixel. Can make the font appear lighter overall.

workbench.fontAliasing.auto.en: Applies `default` or `antialiased` automatically based on the DPI of displays.

workbench.fontAliasing.default.en: Sub-pixel font smoothing. On most non-retina displays this will give the sharpest text.

workbench.fontAliasing.none.en: Disables font smoothing. Text will show with jagged sharp edges.

workbench.hover.delay.en: Controls the delay in milliseconds after which the hover is shown for workbench items (ex. some extension provided tree view items). Already visible items may require a refresh before reflecting this setting change.

workbench.hover.reducedDelay.en: Controls the reduced delay in milliseconds used for showing hovers in specific contexts where faster feedback is beneficial.

workbench.notifications.position.bottom-.en: Show notifications in the bottom left corner.
Show notifications in the bottom right corner.

workbench.notifications.position.top-rig.en: Show notifications in the top right corner, similar to OS-level notifications.

workbench.panel.opensMaximized.always.en: Always maximize the panel when opening it.

workbench.panel.opensMaximized.never.en: Never maximize the panel when opening it.

workbench.panel.opensMaximized.preserve.en: Open the panel to the state that it was in, before it was closed.

workbench.quickOpen.preserveInput.en: Controls whether the last typed input to Quick Open should be restored when opening it the next time.

workbench.reduceMotion.en: Controls whether the workbench should render with fewer animations.

workbench.reduceMotion.auto.en: Render with reduced motion based on OS configuration.

workbench.reduceMotion.off.en: Do not render with reduced motion

workbench.reduceTransparency.en: Controls whether the workbench should render with fewer transparency and blur effects for improved performance.

workbench.reduceTransparency.auto.en: Reduce transparency and blur effects based on OS configuration.

workbench.reduceTransparency.off.en: Do not reduce transparency and blur effects.

workbench.reduceTransparency.on.en: Always render without transparency and blur effects.

workbench.secondarySideBar.defaultVisibi.en: The secondary side bar is hidden by default.
The secondary side bar is visible and maximized by default.
The secondary side bar is visible and maximized by default if a workspace is opened.
The secondary side bar is visible by default.
The secondary side bar is visible by default if a workspace is opened.

workbench.view.showQuietly.en: If an extension requests a hidden view to be shown, display a clickable status bar indicator instead.

wrapTabs.en: Controls whether tabs should be wrapped over multiple lines when exceeding available space or whether a scrollbar should appear instead. This value is ignored when {0} is not set to '{1}'.
comment: {0}, {1} will be a setting name rendered as a link

zenMode.centerLayout.en: Controls whether turning on Zen Mode also centers the layout.

zenMode.fullScreen.en: Controls whether turning on Zen Mode also puts the workbench into full screen mode.

zenMode.hideActivityBar.en: Controls whether turning on Zen Mode also hides the activity bar either at the left or right of the workbench.

zenMode.hideLineNumbers.en: Controls whether turning on Zen Mode also hides the editor line numbers.

zenMode.hideStatusBar.en: Controls whether turning on Zen Mode also hides the status bar at the bottom of the workbench.

zenMode.restore.en: Controls whether a window should restore to Zen Mode if it was exited in Zen Mode.

zenMode.showTabs.en: Controls whether turning on Zen Mode should show multiple editor tabs, a single editor tab, or hide the editor title area completely.

zenMode.showTabs.multiple.en: Each editor is displayed as a tab in the editor title area.

zenMode.showTabs.none.en: The editor title area is not displayed.

zenMode.showTabs.single.en: The active editor is displayed as a single large tab in the editor title area.

zenMode.silentNotifications.en: Controls whether notifications do not disturb mode should be enabled while in Zen Mode. If true, only error notifications will pop out.

newWindowProfile.en: Specifies the profile to use when opening a new window. If a profile name is provided, the new window will use that profile. If no profile name is provided, the new window will use the profile of the active window or the Default profile if no active window exists.

security.allowedUNCHosts.en: A set of UNC host names (without leading or trailing backslash, for example `192.168.0.1` or `my-server`) to allow without user confirmation. If a UNC host is being accessed that is not allowed via this setting or has not been acknowledged via user confirmation, an error will occur and the operation stopped. A restart is required when changing this setting. Find out more about this setting at https://aka.ms/vscode-windows-unc.

security.allowedUNCHosts.patternErrorMes.en: UNC host names must not contain backslashes.

security.restrictUNCAccess.en: If enabled, only allows access to UNC host names that are allowed by the `#security.allowedUNCHosts#` setting or after user confirmation. Find out more about this setting at https://aka.ms/vscode-windows-unc.

agents.voice.handsFree.en: When enabled, voice mode automatically re-enters listening after the assistant finishes speaking, so you can hold a hands-free back-and-forth conversation. When disabled, you start and end each turn manually, and ending the turn sends it. Turns are not ended automatically on trailing silence or a stop phrase unless {0} or {1} is explicitly configured.

agents.voice.language.en: The language used for speech recognition, dictation, and spoken responses. The selectable languages support native voice output. Automatic uses the configured display language for speech recognition and dictation when supported; otherwise, it follows the system or browser locale. English voice output is used when the detected language does not support native voice output. Changing this while voice mode is connected takes effect immediately.

agents.voice.liveTranscript.en: Show your speech as a live, word-by-word transcript while you are speaking. When disabled, your transcript appears only once you finish speaking. Requires `#agents.voice.showTranscript#` to be enabled to be visible.

agents.voice.showButton.en: Controls whether the Voice Mode button is shown in the chat input. When hidden, Voice Mode can still be started with its keyboard shortcut.

agents.voice.showTranscript.en: Show the voice transcript overlay in the chat input area while voice mode is active. Enable this to read responses as text when `#agents.voice.speakResponses#` is disabled.

agents.voice.speakResponses.en: When enabled, the assistant reads responses aloud. When disabled, responses are not spoken; enable `#agents.voice.showTranscript#` to read them as a text transcript instead.

agents.voice.turn.silenceMs.en: Trailing silence in milliseconds before the backend ends the turn automatically. Set to `-1` to disable ending the turn on silence, in which case the turn ends only via a stop phrase ({0}) or manually. When enabled, the backend clamps this to its supported range (currently 200-5000 ms) and is the source of truth. When hands-free mode ({1}) is disabled, the turn is not ended on silence by default unless this setting is explicitly configured, so you keep manual control over when a turn is sent.

agents.voice.turn.silenceMs.disabled.en: Do not end the turn on trailing silence.

agents.voice.turn.stopPhrases.en: Phrases that end the turn when spoken at the end of an utterance. Leave empty to disable ending the turn on a stop phrase, in which case the turn ends only on trailing silence ({0}) or manually. The backend strips the matched phrase from the transcript before it reaches the agent. When hands-free mode ({1}) is disabled, stop phrases do not end the turn by default unless this setting is explicitly configured, so you keep manual control over when a turn is sent.

agents.voice.voice.en: The voice used when the assistant reads responses aloud. Changing this while voice mode is connected takes effect immediately. Use [Voice Mode instructions](command:{0}) to customize Voice Mode behavior and terminology.

chat.agentHostApprovalsPicker.en: When an agent session exposes approval presets, use Tab to reach the Approvals picker and choose how it handles workspace access, commands, and the internet.

chat.agentHostSandboxPolicy.en: In Copilot agent-host sessions, use /sandbox-policy to view the effective sandbox policy. In the response, use Tab to focus Open Sandbox Policy and Enter to open the formatted report.

chat.agentsParallelWork.en: When another Agent Host session is running, a new Agent Host chat may show an invitation to run agents side by side. Only one chat input notification is shown at a time. Use Tab to reach Open Agents Window, Ignore, or Dismiss notification. Open Agents Window copies the current prompt and attachments from that input without sending them or clearing it. An existing draft in the Agents Window is kept. Ignore turns off future invitations; Dismiss notification only hides the invitation for this chat until the window reloads.

chat.announcement.en: Chat responses will be announced as they come in. A response will indicate the number of code blocks, if any, and then the rest of the response.

chat.attachments.inlineReferenceHover.en: To inspect an inline attachment reference, place the cursor on it and invoke Show or Focus Hover{0}. Image references include a preview, while file and folder references include their path.

chat.attachments.inlineReferences.en: To mention an attached context item at a specific position without removing it from the attached context, type # or @ and select the attachment from the suggestions.

chat.attachments.pastedText.en: Long pasted text, including single-line text, is stored as an attached text item and replaced in the input with a numbered inline reference.

chat.attachments.removal.en: To remove attached contexts, focus an attachment and press Delete or Backspace.

chat.completedResponseDisclosure.en: When completed response collapsing is enabled, the final response remains visible while earlier work is collapsed. Use Tab to focus the work disclosure and press Enter or Space to show or hide that work. With persistent progress enabled, a separate file changes button shows lines added and deleted when the collapsed work includes edits. Activate it to open those file changes without expanding the work.

chat.copilotHarnessIntroduction.en: Depending on the active experiment, a new Copilot harness chat may show an introduction to the new Copilot experience when the session starts or after the first request is submitted. Once shown, sending messages does not dismiss it. Use Tab to reach let us know, Learn More, Got it!, or Not Helpful. Learn More opens documentation without hiding the introduction. Got it! and Not Helpful turn off future introductions.

chat.customizationMigrations.en: When workspace customizations need an update, a notice above the new-chat input shows how many need attention. Use Tab to reach Review Migrations and open the Migrations page. Dismiss Migration Notice for This Workspace hides the notice for that workspace, including after restarting, and returns focus to the input. The Customizations toolbar button also announces when migrations are available.

chat.differencePanel.en: The chat view is a persistent interface that also supports navigating suggested follow-up questions, while the quick chat view is a transient interface for making and viewing requests.

chat.differenceQuick.en: The quick chat view is a transient interface for making and viewing requests, while the panel chat view is a persistent interface that also supports navigating suggested follow-up questions.

chat.externalSessionFilter.en: The agent sessions filter includes an External submenu. Use it to choose whether external sessions from another application are shown for the last 24 hours, the last 7 days, always, or not at all.

chat.fileChangesDisclosure.en: File change summaries show the total files, additions, and deletions. Focus the disclosure and press Enter or Space to show or hide the individual files. Focus an additions and deletions label and press Enter or Space to open the changes in a diff editor.

chat.find.en: To search the chat transcript, invoke Find in Chat{0}. Find Next{1} and Find Previous{2} move between results, scrolling each one into view.

chat.focusMostRecentTerminal.en: To focus the last chat terminal that ran a tool, invoke the Focus Most Recent Chat Terminal command{0}.

chat.focusMostRecentTerminalOutput.en: To focus the output from the last chat terminal tool, invoke the Focus Most Recent Chat Terminal Output command{0}.

chat.focusNotice.en: When a tip, notification or introduction appears above the input, toggle focus between it and the chat input{0}.

chat.focusQuestionCarousel.en: When a chat question appears, toggle focus between the question and the chat input{0}.

chat.harnessSwitchFeedbackSurvey.en: After you switch from Copilot to Local, a two-step feedback survey may appear above the chat input. Use Shift+Tab to reach it. In the first step, use Up and Down Arrow to choose why you switched, then press Enter or Space. In the second step, enter any optional feedback and use Tab to reach Submit. Dismiss Survey or Escape closes the survey. After submission, the questions are replaced above the input by a message that your feedback was recorded. Use Dismiss Feedback Acknowledgement or Escape to close it.

chat.inputBlocked.en: When another Codex app is using a conversation, a banner above the input explains how to release it. You can keep editing your draft, but sending is disabled. Quit the app holding the conversation, such as ChatGPT, or exit the Codex CLI session. Use Tab to focus Retry in the banner, then press Enter or Space to check again. Retry does not send your draft.

chat.inspectResponse.en: In the input box, inspect the last response in the accessible view{0}. Thinking content is included in order by default.

chat.inspectResponseThinkingToggle.en: To include or exclude thinking content in the accessible view, run the Toggle Thinking Content in Accessible View command from the Command Palette.

chat.linkContextMenu.en: Focus a link in the chat transcript and press Shift+F10 to open its context menu. Use Copy Link to copy its target. File links with additional editor choices also provide Open With.

chat.mcpStartupSkip.en: When a chat turn is waiting for MCP servers to start, a Skip link may appear. Use Tab to focus Skip and press Enter or Space to continue the turn while those servers start in the background. The current startup message disappears immediately and focus returns to the chat input. New server startups may show another message.

chat.modelPicker.autoMode.en: In the tabbed model picker, the active Copilot tab has an Auto switch beside the provider name. The provider button and switch are separate keyboard targets. Turning Auto on replaces Copilot's individual models with automatic routing choices; provider tabs and search remain available. Turn Auto off to restore the previous manual Copilot model. The switch is disabled when no individual Copilot model is available. Browsing another provider does not change the selected model.

chat.modelPicker.detailsPage.en: In the tabbed model picker, thinking effort and context appear as a configuration button on the hovered, selected, or keyboard-focused model. Use Up and Down Arrow to focus a model, then Tab to reach its configuration button and Enter or Space to open its information and configuration page without selecting it. The button shows Details when no readout is available. Models without configurable settings still open their information page. The thinking effort and context readout beside the model name in the chat input opens the same page for the current model. Opening a configuration button focuses its configuration controls when available. Known values are shown even at their defaults. The Back to Models arrow is beside the model name; navigation and model actions stay at the top while details scroll. Back to Models returns to the previous provider, search, and model list. Escape closes the picker from any page and restores focus.

chat.modelPicker.managedDefault.en: In the tabbed model picker, Org default identifies the model your organization sets for new chats. It remains on that model when you choose another model for this chat; the checkmark identifies your current selection. The Auto section carries the same label when Auto is the organization default.

chat.modelPicker.optimizeFor.en: In Auto mode, use Up and Down Arrow to focus an "Optimize for" preference: Efficiency, Balance, or Intelligence. Enter or Space applies the preference and keeps the picker open. HydraFusion, when available, is an alternative routing choice, not an additional toggle. Focus HydraFusion and press Right Arrow to open its description and focus Learn more. Selecting it clears the active Auto tier; selecting a tier returns to Auto. Turning Auto off preserves the preference and routing choice. Auto has no separate details page: both the Auto name and preference readout in the chat input open these routing choices.

chat.modelPicker.pricingDetails.en: Pricing Details expands in place without moving the model's controls. Expansion and collapse are immediate when reduced motion is enabled. If the details exceed the available space, use Page Up or Page Down while the model details have focus to scroll.

chat.modelPicker.resetToDefault.en: In a model's details, use Tab to reach thinking effort, context, and model actions. Use arrow keys to move between options, then Enter or Space to choose one. Reset to Default appears beside Pin Model when thinking effort or context has been changed. It restores both settings to the model's defaults without changing its pinned state. Choosing an option or resetting the settings selects that model and keeps its details open. Pinning or unpinning updates the model list without moving its details or keyboard focus. Back does not undo saved settings, but a save that finishes after leaving details does not override a newer model selection.

chat.modelPicker.search.en: Type while the model list is focused to search across all providers. In the search field, use Up and Down Arrow to navigate results, Enter to select a model, and Escape to close the picker. Left and Right Arrow move the text cursor.

chat.nextQuestionCarouselQuestion.en: When a chat question is focused, move to the next question{0}.

chat.openTerminalFullOutput.en: When retained full output is available for a completed command, click the output preview to open it in a read-only editor. You can also use the Open Full Output (Read-Only) action in the command header or terminal output Accessible View, or focus the output region and press Enter.

chat.overview.en: The quick chat view is comprised of an input box and a request/response list. The input box is used to make requests and the list is used to display responses.

chat.paste.asText.en: To paste the clipboard as plain text, without converting it to Markdown or storing it as an attachment, invoke Paste as Text{0}.

chat.persistentProgress.en: The chat.experimental.persistentProgress setting defaults to Draw in VS Code Insiders and Off in Stable. Experiments can override either default; an explicit setting takes precedence. Choose Draw, Draw (Monochrome), or Draw (Monochrome, No Icon) to keep a working progress indicator at the bottom until the response finishes. The No Icon variant hides only the decorative VS Code icon; progress text and spoken updates are unchanged. The chat.experimental.persistentProgressVerbosity setting defaults to Compact: tool calls preview while running, then collapse in place to a single summary row when thinking or response text resumes, or the response finishes. Choose Verbose to keep tool chains expanded without a group header or an internal scrolling limit. Use Tab to focus a summary and press Enter or Space to expand or collapse its tool calls. Automatic collapse waits until keyboard focus leaves the group. Completed responses still follow chat.agent.collapseCompletedResponses. Reasoning appears separately as collapsible previews; focus a reasoning header and press Enter or Space to expand or collapse it. Standalone tools keep their decorative icons. Terminal activity animations and subagent pills are unchanged. While the response waits on subagents or background commands, the indicator reports what it is waiting for, including work started in an earlier turn. After 90 seconds without response activity or known background work, it reports that the response is taking longer than usual. Reduced motion disables the collapse animation and keeps the indicator visible without animation. Spoken progress updates are controlled by accessibility.verboseChatProgressUpdates.

chat.persistentProgressHandoff.en: While a response is running, automatically collapsing a reasoning or tool preview keeps a visible header in place. If the header is above the visible content but its details are visible, it moves below the pinned prompt, or to the top of the viewport when there is no pinned prompt. Only the space needed for the visible viewport is reserved. That space is removed when the response finishes or is stopped, after any pending transition and content rendering finish. Expanding a preview consumes reserved space as its content grows. Scrolling to the bottom removes the reserved space. Manual collapses do not add padding. The following response content appears after an automatic collapse finishes. Reduced motion skips this delay. If keyboard focus keeps a preview open, new content continues to appear without waiting for focus to move.

chat.persistentProgressSimplifiedTools.en: With Compact persistent progress, a single tool uses its normal rendering, icon, and details without a group summary or automatic group collapse. MCP tools use the MCP icon. The working indicator reports when chat is waiting for your answers instead of showing a separate question-tool progress row. Question controls remain available, answered questions remain in the response, and question-tool failures remain visible.

chat.persistentReasoningTitles.en: With persistent progress, reasoning headers say Thinking while content arrives. When reasoning finishes, a single heading becomes the header and is removed from the details. Multiple headings remain in the details, with a summary in the header when chat.agent.thinking.generateTitles is enabled and title generation is available.

chat.planReviewEditor.en: When a plan is ready for review, open it from the chat response to edit the plan and add line comments. Use the editor toolbar to navigate, clear, or submit feedback. Choose an implementation action from the plan review in Chat.

chat.previousQuestionCarouselQuestion.en: When a chat question is focused, move to the previous question{0}.

chat.progressVerbosity.en: As the chat request is being processed, you will hear verbose progress updates if the request takes more than 4 seconds. This includes information like searched text for <search term> with X results, created file <file_name>, or read file <file path>. This can be disabled with accessibility.verboseChatProgressUpdates.

chat.readOnlyThinking.en: In read-only chats, thinking details preview while streaming and collapse when finished, regardless of your thinking-style setting. Focus a thinking header and press Enter or Space to expand or collapse its details.

chat.renameSession.en: To rename the current chat session when supported, invoke the Rename command{0}. Agent Host sessions can be renamed after sending the first request.

chat.requestHistory.en: In the input box, use up and down arrows to navigate your request history. Edit input and use enter or the submit button to run a new request.

chat.sandboxUnavailable.en: If the agent host cannot support the configured sandbox, a notification above the input explains why. Use Tab to reach Dismiss notification. Dismissing hides the warning for this session until the window reloads, without changing sandboxing or preventing messages.

chat.sessionArchiveNudge.en: An archive suggestion appears above the chat input when the session's pull requests are merged. Use Tab or Shift+Tab to reach Archive, Configure Automatic Cleanup, or Dismiss Archive Suggestion, then press Enter or Space. Configure Automatic Cleanup opens the settings for automatically archiving inactive merged sessions and permanently deleting automatically archived merged sessions. The explanation under What Does "Archive" Do? is collapsed by default. Use Tab to reach it and Enter or Space to expand or collapse it. Dismissing the suggestion, including with Escape while it is focused, returns to the chat input. Archiving the session hides it from the sessions list so you can focus on your remaining tasks. The session is not deleted. Ask your agent to find it, or look in the "Archived" section of the sessions list. You can unarchive it anytime. The worktree created for the session, if any, will be deleted. You can recreate it by unarchiving the session.

chat.sessionDoneNudge.en: A mark as done suggestion appears above the chat input when the session's pull requests are merged. Use Tab or Shift+Tab to reach Mark as Done, Configure Automatic Cleanup, or Dismiss Mark as Done Suggestion, then press Enter or Space. Configure Automatic Cleanup opens the settings for automatically archiving inactive merged sessions and permanently deleting automatically archived merged sessions. The explanation under What Does "Mark as Done" Do? is collapsed by default. Use Tab to reach it and Enter or Space to expand or collapse it. Dismissing the suggestion, including with Escape while it is focused, returns to the chat input. Marking the session as done hides it from the sessions list so you can focus on your remaining tasks. The session is not deleted. Ask your agent to find it, or look in the "Done" section of the sessions list. You can restore it anytime. The worktree created for the session, if any, will be deleted. You can recreate it by restoring the session.

chat.sessionPreparation.en: While a session is being prepared, a progress message appears in the transcript. Use Tab or Shift+Tab to reach Show Log, when available, and press Enter or Space to open the output log. Use Stop to cancel preparation. The chat input and attachment controls are disabled until preparation finishes.

chat.sessionStatusPills.en: When session status pills appear above the input, use Tab to focus the toolbar, then use the left and right arrow keys to move between pills. Press Enter or Space to activate a pill. Open the context menu{0} to choose which optional pills are visible. Pull Requests Options lets you show all pull requests or only open and draft ones, remembered across sessions. If every pull request is filtered out, these options are also available in any other pill's context menu or the toolbar context menu.

chat.showHiddenTerminals.en: If there are any hidden chat terminals, you can view them by invoking the View Hidden Chat Terminals command{0}.

chat.signals.en: Accessibility Signals can be changed via settings with a prefix of signals.chat. By default, if a request takes more than 4 seconds, you will hear a sound indicating that progress is still occurring.

chat.speechToText.contextMenu.en: To choose a microphone or turn off dictation or Voice Mode, focus the microphone button in the input toolbar and open its context menu{0} (for example Shift+F10).

chat.stickyPromptHeader.en: The prompt you have scrolled past is pinned to the top of the transcript. Activate its title to jump back to that prompt.

chat.subagentPill.en: When a subagent pill appears in a response, use Tab to focus it and press Enter or Space to open that subagent chat.

chat.subagentPills.en: Subagents appear as pills in the response. Use Tab to focus a subagent pill, then Enter or Space to open its chat. If the subagent has no separate chat, Enter or Space expands or collapses its inline details instead. The pill announces its running state and any pending confirmations.

chat.systemNotificationDisclosure.en: Some session status messages have additional details. Use Tab to focus the status message and press Enter or Space to show or hide its details.

chat.terminalOutputReflow.en: Terminal output reflows to fit the chat width by default. Set {0} to false to keep fixed-width previews with horizontal scrolling. This only changes the preview, not the terminal running the command.

chat.toolFailureIcon.en: Failed tool calls use an error icon in place of their normal tool icon. Their content and available actions stay the same. The Accessible View includes the failure reason or terminal exit code when available.

chat.voiceInputMode.agentProgress.en: When the experimental agents.voice.agentProgress setting is enabled, Voice Mode Agent requests may speak brief progress updates while investigating, planning, editing, validating, or recovering from a problem.

chat.voiceInputMode.holdToTalk.en: In manual Voice Mode, the Start or Stop Listening button toggles listening when tapped, or you can press and hold it to talk and release to send. You can also hold the Voice Mode: Hold to Talk keybinding{0} to talk and release to send; this interrupts the assistant to barge in.

chat.voiceInputMode.segmented.en: When the segmented voice input control is enabled, the input toolbar offers Dictation and Voice Mode. A connected hands-free session also offers Mute or Unmute Microphone; manual Voice Mode instead offers Start or Stop Listening, where stopping sends the completed turn. Each button can be focused and activated with Enter or Space.

chat.voiceMode.introduction.en: The first time Voice Mode starts, an introduction appears above the input box. Tab to reach it, then use the arrow keys to move between the available voices; Enter or Space plays a voice and keeps it for future conversations. Its description also contains two links: Settings, which opens the Voice Mode settings, and How It Responds, which opens a file for customizing what the agent says back. Voice Mode stays connected but does not listen while the introduction is open. Press Escape, or activate the Close button, to dismiss it and return to the input box.

chat.vscodePet.en: Type /vscode-pet to show or hide the VS Code pet above the input. One pet appears in whichever editor or Agents window is active. Drag it around the chat with the mouse and release it to drop it, or flick it in any direction to throw it along the gesture before gravity pulls it down. Pointer collisions are ignored for half a second after a drag release. After that, while the pet is falling, move the pointer into it to bounce it upward; pointer movement and where it catches the pet affect the bounce. Sideways and upward travel do not start the bounce counter. A counter beside the pet tracks consecutive bounces and remains for up to five seconds after landing, or until the pet next reacts or interacts. Landing with at least twenty bounces triggers confetti unless reduced motion is enabled. If it falls past the input, a despawn effect appears at the bottom and a respawn effect appears at the top before it automatically returns to the input. Moving the pointer rapidly between the pet’s left and right sides makes it dizzy. With the keyboard, use Tab to focus the pet, then the left and right arrows to make it hop along the input until it reaches an edge. Hold Shift with the left or right arrow to throw it toward a wall; while it is airborne, press Enter or Space to bounce it upward. Rapidly alternate the unmodified arrows to make it dizzy. Press Enter or Space while it is resting to interact with it. When an achievement unlocks, the pet shows a gold star for ten seconds; activate the pet during that time to open Achievements. Open its context menu{0} (for example Shift+F10), use the up and down arrow keys to choose Achievements, Go on the Run, Come Back, Grow, Shrink, Reset Size, Stable Colors, or Insiders Colors, and press Enter to activate the choice. Grow and Shrink change its size in twenty-percent steps, while Reset Size restores its default size. The pet position and selected size are shared across chats and windows and remembered after you restart.

agentHostModePicker.accessibilityHelp.en: When the experimental combined picker is enabled for a Copilot Agent Host session, Tab reaches separate Mode and Permissions buttons. Press Enter or Space on Mode to open the picker with Agent Mode expanded, or on Permissions to open it with Permissions expanded. Each section header shows its current selection, and the opened section initially focuses that selection. Press Enter or Space on a section header to expand or collapse it, or use Right Arrow to expand and Left Arrow to collapse. Hover or keyboard navigation moves the single row highlight without changing the selection until you activate a choice. Focus the Permissions header and press Tab to reach Configure Permissions, which opens the related settings. Use Up and Down Arrow to navigate and Enter to select a mode, permission level, or terminal sandboxing. Assisted permissions is experimental and evaluates risk before running tools. Enterprise policy can disable Assisted permissions and Allow all. When the session's host requires terminal sandboxing, its sandbox toggle is checked and disabled. If your organization permits bypassing, a supported outside-sandbox permission prompt can offer Allow in this Session. After that action succeeds, you can use the toggle to enable sandboxing again. This restriction applies only to that session. Escape closes the picker and returns focus to the button that opened it.
